new.title: Lunch under the wisteria at Café de Peney
new.desc: The Café de Peney at Route d'Aïre-la-Ville 130 in Peney, Satigny, holds a Michelin Bib Gourmand for good-value traditional French cooking. It sits by an arm of the Rhône and is known for its terrace under wisteria.
new.tip: Book for the terrace in spring and summer; price level is moderate.
new.q: Café de Peney, Route d'Aïre-la-Ville 130, Satigny, Genève

new.title: Eat the seasonal lunch menu at Chez Cami in Satigny
new.desc: Chez Cami at Route du Mandement 142 is a family-run village restaurant cooking with fresh local produce and a menu that changes with the seasons, with a list of Geneva wines from regional growers.
new.tip: Open Monday to Friday only, with a daily lunch menu and afterwork sessions Wednesday to Friday from 18:00 to 19:30.
new.q: Chez Cami, Route du Mandement 142, Satigny, Genève

new.title: Dine at Les Curiades in Vieux-Lully
new.desc: Les Curiades at Vieux-Lully 10 in Bernex holds a Michelin Bib Gourmand and has been serving food since 1850. It has a terrace, a wine list of Geneva vintages and vegetarian menus.
new.tip: Book ahead for the terrace and weekends.
new.q: Restaurant Les Curiades, Vieux-Lully 10, Bernex, Genève

new.title: Stop at the Auberge de Dardagny on the wine road
new.desc: The Auberge de Dardagny stands at Route du Mandement 504 in the winegrowing village of Dardagny and serves Swiss and French food, rated 4.3 out of 5 by about 78 Google reviewers, at roughly CHF 30 to 80 a head.
new.tip: Opening hours were not confirmed, so check before going; combine it with the Allondon walk.
new.q: Auberge de Dardagny, Route du Mandement 504, Dardagny, Genève

new.title: Eat on stilts at the Restaurant de la Plage in Eaux-Vives
new.desc: This restaurant and buvette on stilts at Quai Gustave-Ador 75, at the end of the public Eaux-Vives beach, overlooks the Jet d'Eau, the harbour and the open lake. It cooks with local, traceable products and has a Gault&Millau score of 13.
new.tip: Closed Monday and Tuesday; open Wednesday to Saturday 10:00 to 23:00 and Sunday 10:00 to 19:00.
new.q: Restaurant de la Plage, Quai Gustave-Ador 75, Genève

new.title: Have tea and pastries at Wolfisberg on Place du Temple
new.desc: The Boulangerie-Pâtisserie Wolfisberg was founded in 1961 by François Wolfisberg Sr. and grew from a small shop into a bakery with a tea room and a large terrace on Place du Temple in Carouge.
new.tip: Open daily 06:00 to 19:00; the tea room suits families.
new.q: Boulangerie-Pâtisserie Wolfisberg, Place du Temple 5, Carouge, Genève

new.title: Try Russian pirojki at the Pirojki bakery in Carouge
new.desc: Pirojki is a Russian bakery run by Olga Mitireva at rue Louis-de-Montfalcon 2 ter, selling the filled pirojki of its name, tvorog ring doughnuts and charlotte à la russe, and open every day according to Le Temps.
new.tip: The article dates from the opening year, so confirm hours before going.
new.q: Pirojki, Rue Louis-de-Montfalcon 2 ter, Carouge, Genève

new.title: Settle into the Café de la Paix in the Jonction
new.desc: The Café de la Paix at 61 boulevard Carl-Vogt in the Jonction quarter is a restaurant, brasserie and bar in the middle of the district.
new.tip: Founding date unconfirmed; check opening hours with the venue.
new.q: Café de la Paix, Boulevard Carl-Vogt 61, Genève
